chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who divorces his wife while he is absent. He said: His divorce is valid in all cases, and his wife observes the waiting period (iddah) from the day he divorces her.

key_terms.عِدَّةٌ: waiting period (implied by context of تَعْتَدُّ)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on divorce when the husband is absent?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's chain in al-Istibsar clarifies that a divorce pronounced by an absent husband is legally binding (sahih) under all conditions, ensuring the wife's iddah commences immediately from the date of pronouncement. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for resolving disputes regarding the validity of talaq when the husband is traveling or away, emphasizing the finality of the utterance regardless of physical presence.
